items.title: Aflac or MetLife: Which Insurance Dividend Wins for Long-Term Income?
items.summary: Two insurers of nearly identical size built very different income stories this year. One owns a 44-year dividend streak, the other owns the momentum. Which advantage matters more when your retirement paycheck depends on it?

items.title: MetLife Stock: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish?
items.summary: MetLife has outperformed the broader market, supported by strong earnings growth and shareholder returns, while analyst sentiment remains moderately bullish.

items.title: The Companies Selling Life Insurance and Annuities Pay Dividends Too. $55,000 in Each of These 3 Pays $5,451 a Year
items.summary: The insurers that collect your premiums and annuity deposits also send checks back to shareholders every quarter. One of three giants yields nearly twice what another pays, and a Japan sales suspension complicates the picture.

items.title: PFG's Retirement Business Navigates Changing Market Conditions
items.summary: Principal Financial's retirement business benefits from rising contributions and pension risk transfer demand, though margin pressure weighs on earnings.

items.title: Stock Grader Upgrades & Downgrades: MetLife, Allstate, Amazon
items.summary: Two insurers in the same industry went in opposite directions in My Stock Grader this week. MetLife, Inc. (MET) moved up to an A, while Allstate Corporation (ALL) slipped to a B. Both carry an A in Quantitative Grade, so the gap comes from their fundamentals. They were among 194 blue-chip stocks whose ratings changed this week (102 upgrades and 92 downgrades), along with Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), which climbed from a D to a C.
